key_insight: A McDonald-style extractive summarization objective can be formulated as an Ising/QUBO problem and efficiently solved on a CMOS Ising machine, enabling low-latency, energy-efficient sentence selection without full neural models.
problem_solved: Reduce the energy, latency, and hardware demands of extractive summarization for real-time or resource-constrained deployments by moving optimization off CPUs/GPUs and onto a purpose-built CMOS Ising accelerator.
method: Formulate sentence selection (maximize relevance, minimize redundancy) as a pairwise Ising/QUBO optimization (McDonald-style objective).
Map the QUBO onto a CMOS Ising hardware substrate and run annealing/parallel recurrent dynamics to obtain candidate summaries.
Apply lightweight post-processing (thresholding, budget constraints, tie-breaking) to produce final extractive summaries and compare to CPU/GPU baselines on standard benchmarks.
impact: Shows a practical hardware-software co-design path for energy-efficient, low-latency extractive summarization suitable for edge devices and large-scale deployments, lowering the barrier to real-time NLP outside datacenters.

paper_title: Extractive summarization on a CMOS Ising machine
paper_authors: Ziqing Zeng, Abhimanyu Kumar, Chris H. Kim, Ulya R. Karpuzcu, Sachin S. Sapatnekar
